brief: Egypt: Hassan Allam Holding signed on 18 Nov to develop NEVERA, a 36 million sqm tourism and commercial destination on the Middle Ring Road in Giza near the Grand Egyptian Museum, with about 6,000 hotel rooms and shopping districts for international brands; no retail area, investment or dates yet (Maspero, 18 Nov; Business Today Egypt, 19 Nov; Daily News Egypt, 22 Nov).

UAE: Amazon.ae brought its Alexa for Shopping assistant, in beta, into its White Friday sale (19 to 30 Nov) (Gulf Business, 19 Nov), and Digital Dubai and the Dubai Future Foundation published the second Dubai State of AI Report, 'Scaling with Trust' (Gulf News, 21 Nov).
Oman: LuLu opened its second hypermarket in Al Amerat, Muscat Governorate, with dedicated space for Omani products (Times of Oman, 18 Nov).

Malls: Marmara Park AVM's İyilik Kumbarası programme won two US Communitas Awards (Mall Report, 20 Nov), and Mega Alma-Ata put up an interactive New Year toy factory under its dome in Almaty (Kursiv, 20 Nov).

Retail tech: Vusion offered about SEK 980.4m in cash for electronic shelf label maker Pricer, with Pricer's board recommending it (Vusion, 17 Nov), while REWE ended its Pick & Go checkout-free store test in Germany (Lebensmittel Praxis, 17 Nov).

findings.title: Digital Dubai and the Dubai Future Foundation publish the second Dubai State of AI Report, themed 'Scaling with Trust'
findings.summary: Digital Dubai, with the Dubai Future Foundation, launched the second edition of the Dubai State of AI Report 2026, under the theme 'Scaling with Trust', at the AI Retreat held during Dubai Future Week (18 to 21 Nov), Gulf News reported on 21 Nov. The report examines five tensions that governments face as they scale AI and introduces 'Dubai's Emerging Doctrine for an AI-Enabled City', which puts public value ahead of technological novelty and will guide measurement in the 2027 edition. It is separate from the City AI Agent approved on 18 Nov (see 19 Nov).
findings.why: Dubai's government is moving AI from pilots into everyday services, which sets the trust and governance expectations that retailers and mall operators using AI in customer service will be measured against.

findings.title: Marmara Park AVM's İyilik Kumbarası community programme wins two US Communitas Awards
findings.summary: MarmaraPark's İyilik Kumbarası ('goodness box'), a social-solidarity programme run by the Istanbul mall, has won two awards from the US-based Communitas Awards, in the Social Solidarity and Company Sponsored Volunteer Project categories, Mall Report reported on 20 Nov. The programme had earlier won a Silver Stevie in the International Business Awards. The report gives no ceremony date, donation totals or details of how the scheme works.
findings.why: Mall-run community programmes are winning international recognition, a reference point for regional malls' own community work and award entries.

findings.title: Mega Alma-Ata puts up an interactive New Year toy-factory installation under its dome
findings.summary: Kursiv reported on 20 Nov that the Mega Alma-Ata shopping and entertainment centre in Almaty has installed a New Year attraction built as a working toy factory, with moving parts, festive music and buttons that let visitors start processes inside it. Elves in traditional Kazakh costume sort letters and pack gifts, and a reindeer sleigh appears to float under the centre's dome. Most social-media reactions were positive, though some users questioned decorating before the 16 December Independence Day holiday; the article names no organiser, run dates or cost.
findings.why: An early, locally themed interactive installation shows Almaty malls competing on experience for New Year footfall.

findings.company: Hassan Allam Holding (master developer, through Grova Developments); Nevera Egypt for Sustainable Development
findings.title: Hassan Allam Holding to develop NEVERA, a 36 million sqm tourism and commercial destination in west Cairo with retail for international brands
findings.summary: Nevera Egypt for Sustainable Development signed a strategic partnership agreement with Hassan Allam Holding on 18 Nov, in the presence of Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, to develop NEVERA, a 36 million sqm tourism, hospitality, entertainment and commercial destination along the Middle Ring Road in Giza, near Sphinx International Airport, the Giza Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum. Hassan Allam Holding is master developer and will carry out the real estate and hospitality development through its subsidiary Grova Developments. Plans include about 6,000 hotel rooms from three to seven stars (nearly 40% of the rooms targeted around the Pyramids and the museum), shopping districts aimed at international brands, a theme park, a convention centre with exhibition grounds and a high-speed rail station; the project will be built in phases, and no investment value, retail area or dates have been published.
findings.why: A tourism-led destination beside the Grand Egyptian Museum adds international-brand retail to west Cairo's pipeline, though its retail size and timing are not yet known.

findings.title: Amazon.ae brings its Alexa for Shopping AI assistant, in beta, into its 12-day White Friday sale in the UAE
findings.summary: Amazon UAE's White Friday sale runs from 19 to 30 Nov across more than 30 product categories, and Amazon is integrating Alexa for Shopping, its AI shopping assistant recently rolled out in beta for UAE customers, Gulf Business reported on 19 Nov. Free for signed-in Amazon.ae customers in the Amazon Shopping app and on the website, the assistant summarises product information and reviews, compares products, shows up to a year of price history, gives personalised recommendations and helps build baskets through conversational requests; the report does not say it can complete purchases. A HarrisX survey commissioned by Amazon says 85% of UAE shoppers are more likely to buy during sales this season, 75% spend more time reading reviews or checking product details and 71% plan purchases in advance.
findings.why: A conversational shopping assistant is now in front of UAE online shoppers in the peak sales fortnight before the Dubai Shopping Festival, raising expectations of retailer and mall apps on product comparison and price transparency.

findings.title: LuLu opens its second hypermarket in Al Amerat, Muscat Governorate
findings.summary: LuLu has opened its second hypermarket in Al Amerat, in the Al Nahdhah area of Muscat Governorate, Times of Oman reported on 18 Nov. The Wali of Al Amerat, Sheikh Hamad bin Sultan Al Busaidi, inaugurated it in the presence of LuLu Group chairman Yusuffali M.A., who linked the opening to Oman's National Day celebrations; the report gives no opening day and names no host mall. The store has dedicated space for Omani products from local farmers, producers and suppliers.
findings.why: LuLu keeps adding hypermarkets in Muscat's suburban districts after Al Hail (see 14 Oct), a sign of continuing demand for grocery anchors in Oman; the store's size awaits a second source.

findings.entity: Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply
findings.title: Jordan's trade ministry widens market and online checks for White Friday sales and requires prices before and after discount to be shown
findings.summary: Jordan's Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply said on 11 Nov that it is expanding field inspections across the country's markets and monitoring online offers during the White Friday discount season, with a focus on misleading promotions on social media. Traders must clearly show prices before and after the discount with full details, discounts must have documented legal grounds and deceptive tactics are banned. Shoppers can report complaints, violations and misleading advertisements through the ministry's complaint channels; the statement gives no penalties or season dates.
findings.why: Retailers and mall tenants in Jordan running White Friday offers face closer checks on price display and social-media promotions, a recurring customer-trust issue for MECSC's service-quality work.

findings.title: Vusion offers about SEK 980.4m in cash for electronic shelf label maker Pricer, with Pricer's board recommending the offer
findings.summary: VusionGroup announced on 17 Nov a recommended cash offer of SEK 6.00 a share for Sweden's Pricer, valuing all its shares at approximately SEK 980.4 million and about 29.6% above the class B share's close on 16 Nov. Pricer's board unanimously recommends acceptance and its largest shareholder, with about 14.15% of the shares, has irrevocably undertaken to accept; the acceptance period is expected to run from about 8 Dec 2026 to 5 Jan 2027, and completion requires Vusion to own more than 90% of the shares, a condition it may waive. Vusion says more than 780 million of its electronic shelf labels are deployed in 80,000 stores, and Pricer says it has delivered over 380 million to more than 28,000 stores in more than 80 countries.
findings.why: Consolidation among electronic shelf label suppliers affects the technology and pricing choices of Gulf grocers and hypermarkets planning digital shelves and in-store retail media.

findings.title: REWE ends its Pick & Go checkout-free store test in Germany
findings.summary: REWE Group is ending the operational test of Pick & Go, a camera-based format that lets shoppers skip scanning and pay at a terminal by card or cash, in its supermarkets in Germany, the latest of which opened in Hannover in spring 2026, Lebensmittel Praxis reported on 17 Nov. Christoph Eltze, REWE Group's Chief Digital and Technology Officer, said the test's learning goals had been met and the findings will now be evaluated, and that REWE will keep testing computer vision and other automated checkout concepts. Retail Technology Innovation Hub says the project ran with technology provider Trigo from 2021.
findings.why: A large European grocer stepping back from checkout-free stores is a useful signal on the format's economics for Gulf grocers and convenience chains weighing similar technology.

library.title: Requirements for Commercial Complexes and Popular Markets (Arabic)
library.publisher: Ministry of Municipalities and Housing, Saudi Arabia
library.note: PDF opened; month not shown (cover year 1446 AH, 2024; no version number printed). National municipal rules for malls and popular markets: siting in commercial zones, minimum shop and kiosk sizes, corridor widths, first-aid room, prayer areas and management office, no commercial use of basements, civil defence approval before licensing under the Saudi Fire Code (SBC 801) and accessibility under SBC 201, a signage hierarchy, CCTV, and the duties of the management office or owners' association; a children's care centre is required above a size threshold. Use for compliance questions from Saudi mall owners and operators; check for a later revision before quoting it.

library.title: Restaurant Requirements (Arabic)
library.publisher: Ministry of Municipalities and Housing, Saudi Arabia
library.note: PDF opened; month not shown (issued under a ministerial decision dated 15/10/1446 AH, 2025). Rules for restaurants and cafés with and without service, cloud kitchens and food kiosks: licensing, location, minimum areas, parking and signage, building and design, kitchen equipment, food safety and allergen labelling, hygiene and waste, and operations (QR code display, CCTV, electronic payments). Food kiosks may sit in commercial complexes; food courts are not named. Reference for F&B tenant fit-out and compliance questions in Saudi malls.

New: Amazon.ae has brought its Alexa for Shopping assistant, in beta for UAE customers, into its White Friday sale; the report does not say it can complete purchases (Gulf Business, 19 Nov; see 23 Nov). Also: Visa has opened Agentic Ready to merchants, acquirers and payment providers with more than 140 participants, after nine UAE banks and fintechs joined its issuer phase in May (Visa, 17 Nov; see 20 Nov). Also: the EU's proposed Digital Fairness Act (11 Nov) would give consumers a right to human customer service, and Sourcing Journal (16 Nov) reports that it would let shoppers who buy through AI agents set and change the agents' key parameters (see 19 Nov). Also: Daydream's stylist agent can complete purchases through one-click checkout, without the report saying how each purchase is approved (TechCrunch, 17 Nov; see 18 Nov). Also: OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet lets its dots agents complete purchases with tokenised cards and Face ID or fingerprint approval for each purchase, first for some US Pro subscribers, and OpenAI published a Commerce Partner Playbook for retailers (TechCrunch, 13 Nov; see 16 Nov). Also: OpenAI's Businesses in ChatGPT lets companies claim their profiles and add product feeds, with Business Agents first for US online sellers (Reuters, 10 Nov; see 12 Nov). Also: CrediMax and Mastercard will explore agentic commerce for Bahrain merchants, starting with Mastercard's Agent Suite for Merchants (Mastercard, 4 Nov; see 10 Nov), and Zalando launched an agent that buys from other retailers inside its app (Reuters, 3 Nov; see 10 Nov).
